newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil seen 50 cts up, Brent flat to 5 cts up.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil seen 50 cts up, Brent flat to 5 cts up.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures are expected to open about 50 cents higher on Friday and Brent crude is expected to open unchanged to five cents higher, helped by a firm transatlantic arbitrage, dealers said.
June gas oil, which settled at $172.00 a tonne on Thursday, should come in firmer, underpinned by tight spot markets in northwest Europe and talk of refinery run cuts.
Meanwhile July Brent, which settled at $19.49 a barrel on Thursday, traded at $19.50 in Singapore on Friday and should hold that level in early London dealing, brokers said.
"There's good support from the arbitrage," said one.
Dealers said Brent would also draw some modest support from news of lower North Sea Forties loadings in June.
The June programme schedules just over five million barrels, or 10 standard 500,000-barrel cargoes fewer than in May. A heavy programme of maintenance is expected to cut into volumes, traders said.
But others had been expecting an even lower figure and suggested the market impact would be limited.
"There has been a lot of focus on Forties in June with some people believing it would be much lower. I wouldn't say this news is bearish but it's probably neutral," said one.
Brokers said the wide open arbitrage to the United States, supported by a robust Brent-WTI July spread of around $1.80 a barrel, was proving more significant.
Gas oil dealing was expected to be light with warm weather forecast for the extended holiday weekend in much of mainland Europe.
But the prompt June/July contango could narrow amid talk of tighter second half May supply, brokers said.
"The prompt physical market is tight, so the contango looks a little artificial. I think it's due a correction," said one.
